sentences.text: 2 4. The petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 3, who are sought to be prosecuted for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, are before this Court.
The registration of the FIR for the aforesaid offences is impugned in this petition.

5. The case of the prosecution is that, the accused No.1 is the husband of the respondent No.2, and the accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents-in-laws of the respondent No.2, and they subjected the respondent No.2 to cruelty both mentally and physically, and a demand was made to bring money from the parental home.
6. The petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 3 are present through video conferencing, and the respondent No.2 - informant is physically present before this Court.

7. A joint memo is filed duly signed by the learned counsel for the petitioners, and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 as well as the respondent No.2 stating that, they have amicably settled the dispute among themselves, and the respondent No.2 has no objection for quashing the impugned FIR.
The joint memo is placed on record.

8. Though the offences are cognizable and non- compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that, the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves, and the respondent No.2 having agreed to withdraw all the allegations made by her, it would be futile exercise if the NC:
2023:KHC:28649 petitioners - accused are subjected to trial, since the probability of their conviction is remote and bleak in view of the settlement.
Hence, the continuation of criminal proceeding will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned FIR in Crime No.0277/2022 registered by the Basavanagudi Women Police Station, is hereby quashed.

Sd/-
